builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: S$^{2}$-PINN: Stochastic Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: S2-PINN replaces classical spectral solvers and monolithic physics-informed neural networks for uncertainty quantification of random PDEs by combining a learnable Gaussian spatial dictionary, Fourier temporal features, a generalized polynomial chaos stochastic basis, and a low-rank CP tensor core trained with a hybrid strong-form and Galerkin-projected residual loss. Its cost is a specialized architecture and training pipeline tied to PDE-residual losses, requiring problem-specific PDE formulations and hyperparameter tuning rather than general-purpose model serving. It can fail when the governing PDE or its stochastic parameterization is misspecified, when residuals are stiff or poorly balanced between loss terms, or when the separable low-rank assumption does not hold for the target solution.
rationale: The method targets scientific UQ for random PDEs, which is outside the production inference, training-efficiency, or agent workflows of a typical AI/ML engineer with constrained infrastructure.
technique: Stochastic separable PINN for random-PDE uncertainty quantification

Its cost is a specialized architecture and training pipeline tied to PDE-residual losses, requiring problem-specific PDE formulations and hyperparameter tuning rather than general-purpose model serving. It can fail when the governing PDE or its stochastic parameterization is misspecified, when residuals are stiff or poorly balanced between loss terms, or when the separable low-rank assumption does not hold for the target solution.

Outperforms nine baselines on mean and variance accuracy and calibration across manufactured random-PDE benchmarks while using significantly fewer parameters; no single multiplicative factor is stated in the abstract.
